Graph of a Filtered Parameter

Source: R/plot_structural.R
plot_filter.Rd

Selects the graph of the path that a score-driven term (modelterms7::gas()) gives to the parameter of its equation: the filtered parameter over the order of the series, with a pointwise confidence band, and optionally the observed response beside it. A model in which several equations carry a gas() term joins them in one filter, and the graph then has a panel for each of the filtered equations.

Usage

plot_filter(
  level = 0.95,
  scale = "response",
  response = FALSE,
  groups = NULL,
  vcov_type = bayesian_vcov(),
  legend = TRUE
)

Arguments

level

The confidence level of the band.

scale

"response" (the default), the parameter, or "link", the predictor.

response

Whether to draw the observed response. It is drawn on the scale of the parameter, so it requires scale = "response", a response that is a vector, and a term in one equation.

groups

NULL for every group, or the labels of the groups to draw (the levels of the by variable as text).

vcov_type

A vcov_method object, the variance of the band.

legend

Whether to draw the legend that names the elements of the graph.

Value

A PlotFilter object, inheriting from term_plot.

Details

The path is the fitted parameter \(\theta_t = g^{-1}(\eta_t)\), where \(\eta_t\) is the static predictor plus the level of the filter, and the band is the interval of predict.StatmodFit() with se = TRUE, which differentiates the filter in the coefficients and in the parameters of the term (the standard error of a filtered predictor). The horizontal axis is the variable named by time in the term, or the row order when it has none.

For a panel (gas(by = id)) the graph has one panel for each group, at most twelve; with more groups, groups names the ones to draw.

See also

autoplot.StatmodFit(), plot_news_impact()

Examples

set.seed(4)
n <- 100
x <- rnorm(n)
f <- 0
y <- integer(n)
for (t in seq_len(n)) {
  lam <- exp(0.7 + 0.3 * x[t] + f)
  y[t] <- rpois(1, lam)
  f <- 0.15 * (y[t] - lam) * lam^(-0.5) + 0.8 * f
}
dd <- data.frame(t = seq_len(n), x = x, y = y)
fit <- statmod(y ~ x + gas(p = 1, q = 1, time = t, scaling = 0.5),
               distributions7::poisson_distrib(), dd)
ggplot2::autoplot(fit, term = "gas(p = 1, q = 1, time = t, scaling = 0.5)",
                  plot_type = plot_filter(response = TRUE))
